literal: Treatise on Camps and Guards, Part 1
idiomatic: Treatise on Camps and Guards, Part 1

literal: In high antiquity's age, grass clothes and tree food, nesting in trees and dwelling in caves, happy and at ease, not seeking and not striving.
idiomatic: In high antiquity people wore grass and ate from trees, nested in trees and dwelt in caves, happy and at ease, neither seeking nor striving.

literal: From when the Flame Emperor's government declined, Chiyou made disorder, and weapons were first made to poison all under heaven.
idiomatic: From when the reign of the Flame Emperor declined and Chiyou raised disorder, weapons were first fashioned to poison the realm.

literal: The Yellow Emperor arose and executed him at the slope of Zhuolu.
idiomatic: When the Yellow Emperor arose, he slew him at the foot of Zhuolu.

literal: At rest then elephant tusks in the palace; on the march then yak tails hung on the banners, taking this as a warning to all under heaven for ten thousand generations.
idiomatic: At rest he displayed elephant tusks in the palace; on the march he hung yak tails on the banners, as a warning to all under heaven for ten thousand generations.

literal: Thus armies, camps, and guards could not but be established.
idiomatic: Thus armies, camps, and guards had to be established.

literal: South of Ji prefecture, passing through the flood's transformation, the Xia ruler first made walls and cities.
idiomatic: South of Ji prefecture, after the transformation wrought by the Great Flood, the Xia first established walls and cities.

literal: Its people settled natively and dwelt within the pacified domain, outward exerting military guard, inward aligning civil teaching, keeping defense on the four borders.
idiomatic: Its people settled as natives within the pacified domain, exerting military guard without and aligning civil teaching within, keeping defense on the four borders.

literal: The establishment of camps and guards was only to prepare against the unexpected.
idiomatic: The establishment of camps and guards was only to prepare for the unexpected.

literal: North of Bing and Ying, fierce winds and much cold; following the yang they migrated, years without peaceful dwelling, vast earth ten thousand li, bandits and villains seizing gaps to act.
idiomatic: North of Bing and Ying, fierce winds and bitter cold; following the sun they migrated, year without settled dwelling, vast earth ten thousand li, bandits and villains seizing gaps to act.

literal: The establishment of camps and guards was taken as the constant norm.
idiomatic: The establishment of camps and guards was taken as the norm.

literal: Such was the tendency.
idiomatic: Such was the situation.

literal: From when Liao first grew great, its institutions were especially dense.
idiomatic: When Liao first grew great, its institutions were especially dense.

literal: In residence there were palace guards, called orudo; on departure there were traveling camps, called napo;
idiomatic: In residence there were palace guards, called orudo (mobile palace encampments); on departure there were traveling camps, called napo (imperial seasonal encampments);

literal: Distributed to guard the border marches, called tribal divisions.
idiomatic: distributed to guard the frontiers, called tribal divisions.

literal: When there was business then attack and battle were the task; in leisure then hunting and fishing were the livelihood.
idiomatic: When there was business, attack and battle were the task; in leisure, hunting and fishing were the livelihood.

literal: No day without camping, no place without guarding.
idiomatic: No day without camping, no place without guarding.

literal: In the scale of founding a state, nothing was heavier than this.
idiomatic: In the scale of founding a state, nothing weighed more than this.

literal: They composed the "Treatise on Camps and Guards."
idiomatic: The "Treatise on Camps and Guards" was composed.

literal: ○ Palace Guards
idiomatic: ○ Palace Guards

literal: Liao state's law: when the Son of Heaven took the throne, palace guards were set up, prefectures and counties divided, tribal divisions analyzed, government offices established, household registers recorded, troops and horses prepared.
idiomatic: Liao law: when the Son of Heaven assumed the throne, palace guards were established, prefectures and counties divided, tribal divisions analyzed, government offices set up, household registers made, and troops and horses prepared.

literal: On demise the entourage followed the empress and consorts' palace tents to serve the imperial tomb.
idiomatic: On death the entourage followed the empress and consorts' palace tents to attend the imperial tomb.

literal: When there were levies, able-bodied men followed military affairs and old and weak remained on guard.
idiomatic: When levies were issued, able-bodied men followed military affairs while the old and weak remained on guard.

literal: Taizu was called Hongyi Palace, Empress Yingtian was called Changning Palace, Taizong was called Yongxing Palace, Shizong was called Jiqing Palace.
